calibration.method: Platt (sigmoid) on raw margin, fit on train out-of-fold scores

cost_definition: total = c * (number flagged, true or false alerts) + sum(Amount of every missed, unflagged fraud)

costs.currency: EUR (matches dataset Amount); ALL VALUES HYPOTHETICAL, not PayGuard operating costs

decision_rule: Rule B: flag if calibrated_p > c / mean_fraud_amount_train

deviation_from_preregistered_rule.original_rule_A: flag if calibrated_p * Amount > c (frozen provisionally in v1, hash in superseded_v1_config.sha256)
deviation_from_preregistered_rule.replaced_by: Rule B (above), approved by the user after Stage 2a validation results
deviation_from_preregistered_rule.unchanged: models, hyperparameters, preprocessing, seeds, split, OOF folds, Platt calibrators
deviation_from_preregistered_rule.why_A_rejected: On validation, Rule A cost XGBoost EUR 1,726 at c=5 vs ~EUR 630 for in-sample reference cutoffs and flagged 309 transactions (median Amount ~EUR 1k) with expected prevented loss (~EUR 11.9k) above the total validation fraud value (EUR 8.4k): it relied on amount-conditional calibration that was only checked in aggregate.

xgboost.scale_pos_weight: negatives/positives of the training data it is fit on

preprocessing.logreg: StandardScaler fit on the data passed to fit (train only) inside a Pipeline

rule_assumptions: calibrated fraud probability (aggregate; not verified per Amount band)
constant review cost c per flagged transaction (hypothetical)
every fraud costs the TRAIN mean fraud Amount if missed (a single constant; real fraud sizes are highly skewed)
a flagged fraud is fully prevented

split.rule: sort by Time (stable); cut at Time values found at 70% and 85% row positions; ties go to the later split
split.test: not accessed during Stage 2a (only its start time is read from the Time column)
